chapter: Garland: early Ory band and bass craft
title: Brass-band funeral instruments and Black Benny
summary: Garland says what he played in funeral bands (alto horn, bass drum) and recalls Black Benny as the band's tough protector.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: And at the funeral you played, what did you play drums?
I played, no. I played drums too, but I played alto horn. Or alto horn.

We used to say peck horn. Yeah, it was a round one. No, not a mellow one. Peck horn. Straight up there. Straight up there. Straight up there. Yeah, straight up there. You didn't have laughter beats. That, that, da-da-da-da-da. I used to play peck horn. About the same as the snare drum part.
He played, he played good, a mellow phone player. He played mellow phone too, huh? He was a pretty good alto player, yeah. Who played bass drum in that? I guess Henry Martin played snare drum.

I used to play bass drum most of the time, but when we were in the big band up, I'd play alto. Finally, I got, we used to let Black Benny play bass drum. Yeah. You heard of him, didn't you? Oh, yes. Yeah.
Yeah. Right Benny was playing. Armstrong, this Armstrong's always talking about. Yeah.

It was one of his players. Yeah, it was. He used to fight for the band. He'd go out and fight for the band. Nobody wouldn't do us nothing. He used to take care of us. He was a tough one. He was tough too. He liked to fight. He loved to fight.
